clue.text: Nurse in hospital needing a degree first

indicators.note: the words 'a degree' are said to come first, ahead of the hospital letter

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a university degree
H is the standard map and sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A nurse working in a hospital needs a university degree before starting.
explanation.walkthrough: An amah is a nurse or nanny in parts of Asia, a word met mostly in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: An amah is a wet-nurse or children's nurse in South and East Asia, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Like a gale that has son coming in dishevelled

indicators.note: the son's letter comes in among the letters for windy, so it goes inside them

parts.note: windy weather that is like a gale is blowy
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Someone describes a windswept scene where a son arrives looking messy.
explanation.walkthrough: Blowsy (also blowzy) describes a woman who looks red-faced and untidy.
explanation.definitionFit: Blowsy means coarse and untidy in appearance, so it is a near-synonym of dishevelled.

clue.text: Easily accessible study that is supplied with holy books archdeacon enters

indicators.note: the archdeacon's title enters the string of study, that is and holy books, so it sits within them

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
i.e., id est, means 'that is'
NT is the New Testament, a collection of holy books
Ven, Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: A study room is stocked with Bibles, and a senior cleric walks in.
explanation.walkthrough: Ven, short for Venerable, is the courtesy title for an archdeacon in the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Something convenient is handy and close to hand, so it is easily reached or accessible.

clue.text: Like some chemical container overturned, getting grass stunted

indicators.note: in a down clue the container is turned over, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: a tin is a metal container

indicators.note: stunted growth is cut short, so the grass loses its last letter

parts.note: rice is a cereal grass

explanation.surface: A container is knocked over and the grass beneath it grows stunted, as if poisoned by chemicals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' turns TIN into NIT, and 'stunted' trims RICE to RIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitric describes compounds containing nitrogen, as in nitric acid, so it fits an adjective for a chemical.

clue.text: This powder? Somehow manages to get one settled inside

indicators.note: the numeral is settled in the middle of the rearranged letters
somehow suggests things done in some unknown way, so the letters of manages are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone manages to get settled by taking a powder, perhaps for indigestion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' rearranges MANAGES to MAGNESA, and 'settled inside' places I between S and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnesia, magnesium oxide, is a white powder taken as an antacid or laxative.

clue.text: Where the Abraham Heritage fans want to go round?

parts.words: Where the Abraham Heritage fans want
parts.note: Ur of the Chaldees was the birthplace of Abraham, so fans of his heritage would want to visit it

explanation.surface: A question asks where enthusiasts for Abraham's legacy hope to travel on their trip.
explanation.walkthrough: Fans of Abraham's heritage want to go to UR, his biblical home city, which reads as TO UR.
explanation.definitionFit: A round, such as a postman's or a doctor's, is a circuit of visits, which is a trip of that kind.

clue.text: Girl given brief part, being hugged by Michael on screen?

indicators.note: the shortened part is held within the actor's surname

parts.note: Michael Caine is a famous film actor

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the part loses its last letter

parts.note: an actor's part is a role

explanation.surface: A young actress gets a small role in a film, in a scene where Michael Caine embraces her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on screen' tells the solver this Michael is the film actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Caroline is a female first name, so it is an example of a girl's name.

clue.text: Around end of October person at races may be one beset by leaves

indicators.note: the racecourse person is placed around that final letter

parts.note: a bookmaker takes bets at racecourses

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, taken here from October

explanation.surface: In late October, a racecourse bookie is surrounded by falling autumn leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes into BOOKMAKER after the A. 'leaves' looks like autumn foliage but means the pages of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A marker kept in a book sits between its pages, so it is surrounded by leaves of paper.

clue.text: Much beastly noise interrupted by officer

indicators.note: the officer breaks into the cow's noise, so goes inside it

parts.note: a moo is the noise a cow makes
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: An officer cuts across a great deal of animal noise.
explanation.walkthrough: Molto is the Italian musical direction for 'very' or 'much'.
explanation.definitionFit: Molto is a musical term meaning very or much, as in molto allegro.

clue.text: Lover travelling to Romania

indicators.note: travelling suggests moving about, so the letters of to Romania move into a new order

explanation.surface: A lover is off on a trip to Romania.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorato is a male lover, from the Italian word for one in love.

clue.text: Beyond the low hill it's always still

indicators.note: the word for always comes beyond, after, the hill

parts.note: a how is a low hill or burial mound, a northern English word
ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'

explanation.surface: Past the small hill, all is forever calm and quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' looks like calm, but is the adverb meaning 'nevertheless'.
explanation.definitionFit: Still, used as 'even so' or 'nevertheless', is a synonym of the contrasting adverb.

clue.text: Part of England terribly forlorn with one king briefly ousting another

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so the letters are jumbled
the king's K pushes out one of the R letters and takes its place

parts.note: R, for rex, is another abbreviation for king
K is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Somewhere in England is dreadfully sad, as one king is soon pushed aside by a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: FORLORN has two Rs; 'ousting' swaps one for K, and 'terribly' rearranges the result. Norfolk is a county in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Norfolk is an English county on the east coast, so it is a part of the country.

clue.text: Material being worn by man

parts.note: Ray is a man's name
clothes being worn are on

explanation.surface: A fabric is being worn by a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Rayon is a synthetic fabric made from cellulose, so it is a type of material.

clue.text: Words sung in ground before Italian musical coming up

indicators.note: the ground comes before the other pieces

parts.note: rec is short for recreation ground, a public park

indicators.note: in a down clue the musical comes up, so its letters read upwards

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical

explanation.surface: Song lyrics are performed on a field ahead of an Italian show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns EVITA into ATIVE. A rec is a British public park or sports field.
explanation.definitionFit: Recitative is the speech-like singing in opera that carries the dialogue, so it is text that is sung.

clue.text: Not the only big name in charge of a country

parts.note: a co-star shares top billing, so is not the only star

explanation.surface: A celebrity who shares the spotlight is put in charge of a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Costa Rica is a Central American republic, so it is a country.

clue.text: Walk, showing affection, full of endless silly talk

indicators.note: the affectionate word is filled with the shortened silly talk

parts.note: amatory means expressing love

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the silly talk loses its last letter

parts.note: bull is nonsense talk

explanation.surface: A romantic stroll is filled with endless nonsense chat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Walk' looks like a verb but is a noun: a cloister walkway.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambulatory is a covered walkway in a cloister or around a church apse, so it is a walk.

clue.text: Remarkable comic dancing around in brief TV film?

indicators.note: dancing around suggests moving about freely, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A brilliant comedian prances about in a short television film.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows the definition is playful: an advert is a short film on TV.
explanation.definitionFit: A commercial break is the slot of advertisements, short films shown between programmes on television.

clue.text: Like a gentle female that could make man yield

indicators.note: the letters of man yield could be made into another word, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A gentle woman's manner could make a man give in.
explanation.definitionFit: Maidenly means typical of a young unmarried woman: modest, gentle and shy.

clue.text: Teller of many a story — companion gets uplift lapping it up

parts.note: CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

indicators.note: the rise laps around the reversed word, holding it inside

parts.note: a rise is an uplift

indicators.note: in a down clue the word it reads upwards, so its letters reverse

explanation.surface: A storyteller's friend is cheered as everyone eagerly drinks in the tales.
explanation.walkthrough: Agatha Christie wrote dozens of crime novels; the Companion of Honour is a British order whose members put CH after their name.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie wrote over sixty detective novels, so she told many a story.

clue.text: The heartless leftie pursuing fool talked tremulously

indicators.note: the shortened word and the leftie pursue, so follow, the fool

parts.note: a twit is a fool

indicators.note: heartless means losing the central letter, so the word The loses its middle

parts.note: a red is a left-winger

explanation.surface: A cold left-winger chasing an idiot spoke shakily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the H from THE, leaving TE.
explanation.definitionFit: To twitter is to speak in a quick, nervous, trembling way, like birds' chirping.

clue.text: Get rid of seedy bars? Town's first requirement

parts.note: a dive is a disreputable bar

indicators.note: the first letter of Town's is taken

explanation.surface: A town's top priority is to close down its sleazy drinking spots.
explanation.definitionFit: To divest is to strip or dispose of something, such as shares, so it means to shed.

clue.text: Hungry boy denied nothing gets meat

indicators.note: the boy is denied the nothing letter, so it is taken away

parts.note: Oliver Twist famously asked for more food
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A hungry lad, refused nothing, gets some meat.
explanation.walkthrough: In Dickens's novel the starving Oliver Twist asks for more gruel.
explanation.definitionFit: Liver is an organ eaten as offal, so it is a kind of meat.

clue.text: Bag is stowed in the course of farewell

indicators.note: the word is is stowed within the farewell, placed in its middle

parts.note: vale is Latin for farewell

explanation.surface: A bag is packed away while someone says goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: A valise is a small travelling case, so it is a type of luggage.

clue.text: Culprit, remorseful, showing signs of nervousness?

indicators.note: the letters are showing inside the words culprit remorseful, spanning the comma

explanation.surface: A guilty wrongdoer, full of remorse, displays nervousness.
explanation.definitionFit: Tremors are shakes or quivers, and shaking hands are a sign of being nervous.

clue.text: Horned animal making men cross — ultimately they may get impaled

indicators.note: the last letter is stuck between the other pieces, pierced by them

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers
X is the shape of a cross

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter of they is taken

explanation.surface: A horned beast angers men, who may end up gored on its horns.
explanation.walkthrough: Y goes between OR and X.
explanation.definitionFit: An oryx is a large antelope with long, straight horns.

clue.text: Against getting left in the country essentially

parts.note: v, versus, means against

indicators.note: the left letter is put in the country

parts.note: Italy is a country

explanation.surface: Someone opposes being stranded in their homeland, which is basically the point.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitally means in a way that is of essential importance, so both mean fundamentally.

clue.text: Jerk who lives across the pond?

definitions.meaning: a sudden sharp pull or tug
the pond is the Atlantic, so this means an American, in British slang

explanation.definitionFit: Yank is both a sharp pull and British slang for an American, who lives across the Atlantic.

clue.text: Goddesses featured in prayer included by backward-looking east European

indicators.note: the prayer is included inside the reversed Slav
backward-looking means the Slav's letters read in reverse

parts.note: a Slav is a person from eastern Europe
the Kyrie is a prayer of the Mass

explanation.surface: Goddesses appear in a prayer said by a nostalgic eastern European.
explanation.walkthrough: The Kyrie eleison ('Lord, have mercy') is a short prayer in the Christian liturgy.
explanation.definitionFit: Valkyries are Norse warrior maidens, minor goddesses who chose the slain in battle.

clue.text: Engineers provided with wrong sticky stuff

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
a sin is a wrong

explanation.surface: Engineers are supplied with the wrong kind of glue.
explanation.definitionFit: Resin is a gummy substance from trees, so it is sticky material.
